    Aggressive 40% discounting: +31% short-term signups, -12% retention churn. Unsustainable long-term play. Standard SMB segment.

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two degradations (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are causally linked: onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly addresses both, while activation messaging treats the downstream symptom only. Inherited memory supports this direction twice (memory_31: signup field reduction lifted first-week activation durably; memory_86: shorter onboarding improved completion and time-to-value). I explicitly decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that aggressive discounting bought +31% signups at -12% retention churn, which is directly adverse to the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not touch the observed funnel decay; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the price-sensitive SMB accounts being lost. I am verifying memory_31 because its 'durable lift' claim is the load-bearing one and consolidated summaries strip effect sizes, observation windows, and segment definitions - and because cutting required signup fields is precisely the intervention that can raise raw activation while degrading lead qualification data, sales routing, and therefore *qualified* revenue downstream. I need the original record to see whether qualified-revenue or lead-quality metrics were ever measured, or whether only activation was. I verify memory_91 as the strongest alternative, so that if memory_31's durability does not survive inspection I can switch on evidence rather than re-derive from summaries. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the memories are day-12 to day-61 records under pre-competitor conditions and may not transfer to the current mix; the slot does not carry over, so I size to detect a real effect while holding a downstream guardrail on lead quality and qualified pipeline, not just top-of-funnel activation. If verification shows memory_31 measured only activation with no downstream quality check, I will narrow to onboarding-length reduction per memory_86 (which does not touch qualification fields) rather than cutting signup fields.
